messages.author: 4b4a7b00c1dd09c7
messages.subject: Re: Model fit
parts:
Hi Chris (and list),

There is plenty of discussion and examples showing how to choose detection
function models in the Distance Sampling book, which is available for free
online (http://www.ruwpa.st-and.ac.uk/distancebook/ see, for example, section
3.5 "Choice of model", sections 4.1-4.6, 5.1-5.6, 8.2, 8.3, etc). If this
still doesn't make sense you may want to think about coming on a workshop (next
ones will be August 2001 in St Andrews http://www.ruwpa.st-and.ac.uk/icods/).

I'm not sure what you meant about not being able to generate graphs of model
fits for your data in Distance. I assume you mean Distance 3.5. Running
analyses in Distance 3.5 is explained in the online manual, under Analyses in
Distance and subsequent pages.

Hope this helps. If you have specific questions, send them to me rather than
the list and I will respond privately.

- Len Thomas
Distance project coordinator

--
Len Thomas (l...@mcs.st-and.ac.uk)
Research Unit for Wildlife Population Assessment
Mathematical Institute, University of St Andrews
Scotland
